metadata_tier.py is introduced as a genuinely new, dependency-free module.
The diff header presents metadata_tier.py as a new file.
The module imports nothing from the package and nothing from nicegui, so no cycle is possible.
outlier_attrs computes the relative gap against the larger value and cannot divide by zero.
Measured values arriving as strings are converted before comparison, and a non-numeric value cannot raise.
OUTLIER_BAND is 0.01 and is the single constant both the CLI listing and the preview listing read.
An editorial divergence still produces a conflict carrying its full attribute set.
A group with at least one divergent editorial attribute still raises a conflict and can still take a resolution, an on_conflict policy or the unresolved abort.
That group's attrs holds every divergent attribute, measured ones included.
A group divergent on measured attributes alone produces no ConflictRow and cannot reach the unresolved abort.
A group divergent on both tiers is not also listed as an outlier, so no group is reported twice.
SettledRow carries the identity key, the divergent measured attribute names, the per-member values, the winning record's primary key and the outlier readings.
A tiered attribute still travels with the winning record into the written output.
divergent_attrs still contains the tiered measured attributes where entry_patches reads it.
The written entry carries the winner's measured values, never base's silently retained number.
settled_rows is present on every run including a clean one, and groups_settled_by_rule and settled_groups_outlying are derived from that list rather than counted separately.
_handle_splice prints groups_settled_by_rule with the stats and one outlier line per outlying settled row read off result.settled_rows; a run that settled nothing prints no listing.
The reconstruct_report.py path is settled: the plan places it under traktor_nml/gui/ while the entry-point contract names traktor_nml/.
settled_sentence states the count read off the model and names the record the answer was taken from.
OutlierRow carries no candidate reference and no decision state, so it cannot be mistaken for a decidable row.
